destination.name: Warrnambool
destination.tagline: South-west Victoria's largest town, with shipwreck history and a volcano reserve
destination.description: Warrnambool is the largest town in south-west Victoria, about 260 km west of Melbourne, and is sometimes treated as the end of the Great Ocean Road. Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum has a replica maritime village and a night show telling the story of the Loch Ard wreck. Tower Hill, 14 km west, is an extinct volcano that erupted at least 34,000 years ago and is now a wildlife reserve. A 37 km rail trail links the town with Port Fairy via Koroit.
whyVisit: Watch southern right whales from shore
Learn shipwreck history at a maritime village
Walk the rim of an extinct volcano

goodToKnow.title: Whale season June-September
goodToKnow.detail: Southern right whales visit Logans Beach from June to September. Check the visitor centre for confirmed sightings.

goodToKnow.title: Allow time to drive
goodToKnow.detail: Melbourne is about 3.5 hours by the Princes Highway and longer along the Great Ocean Road, so plan an overnight.
